Retrieve row index for a set of features

Source: R/celda_functions.R
retrieveFeatureIndex.Rd

This will return indices of features among the rownames or rowData of a data.frame, matrix, or a SummarizedExperiment object including a SingleCellExperiment. Partial matching (i.e. grepping) can be used by setting exactMatch = FALSE.

Usage

retrieveFeatureIndex(
  features,
  x,
  by = "rownames",
  exactMatch = TRUE,
  removeNA = FALSE
)

Arguments

features

Character vector of feature names to find in the rows of x. Features that are NA never match.

x

A data.frame, matrix, or SingleCellExperiment object to search.

by

A single character string. Where to search for features in x. If set to "rownames" then the features will be searched for among rownames(x). If x inherits from class SummarizedExperiment, then by can be one of the fields in the row annotation data.frame (i.e. one of colnames(rowData(x))). Default "rownames".

exactMatch

Boolean. Whether to only identify exact matches or to identify partial matches using grep. Default TRUE.

removeNA

Boolean. If set to FALSE, features not found in x will be given NA and the returned vector will be the same length as features. If set to TRUE, then the NA values will be removed from the returned vector. Default FALSE.

Value

A vector of row indices for the matching features in x.

See also

'retrieveFeatureInfo' from package 'scater' and regex for how to use regular expressions when exactMatch = FALSE.

Author

Yusuke Koga, Joshua Campbell

Examples

# A small count matrix with 20 genes and 10 cells
counts <- matrix(seq_len(200), nrow = 20, ncol = 10,
                 dimnames = list(paste0("Gene_", 1:20),
                                 paste0("Cell_", 1:10)))

# Find genes by their exact names
retrieveFeatureIndex(c("Gene_1", "Gene_5"), counts)
#> [1] 1 5

# Find genes by part of their names
retrieveFeatureIndex(c("ne_5", "ne_7"), counts, exactMatch = FALSE)
#> [1] 5 7
